newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile can support two new copper smelters - Sonami.
newsitem.headline: Chile can support two new copper smelters - Sonami.

text.p: Chile's booming copper industry will churn out enough copper concentrates in coming years to supply two new smelters which are under currently under study, said trade group National Mining Society (Sonami).
"It's probable that there is justification for two smelters," said president Hernan Hochschild. "One in the extreme north of the country and another further south."
Sonami started work two months ago on a study for South Korean industrial giant Hyundai on the feasibility of building a smelter which would process 400,000 tonnes of copper concentrates a year.
The report has been delayed and should be ready in March, three months later than originally expected, he said.

Last week Chilean electricity giant Endesa announced it has struck a deal with Finland's Outokumpu Oy to study the construction of $800 million smelter to process one million tonnes of copper concentrates.
Although Endesa and Outokumpu have not said where they intend to build their plant, it is likely to in the northern First or Second Regions.
Outokumpu officials have said the company has had talks on supply contracts with the huge Escondida mine and the new Collahuasi pit which will start operating in 1998.
Rising copper production in the more southern Third to Fifth Regions, including the expansion of the Los Pelambres pit, could make a second smelter viable, said Hochschild.
"We have no doubt that between the Third and Fifth Regions... the rising supply of concentrates make more smelter capacity feasible," he said.
Figures from government copper studies center Cochilco show Chilean production of copper concentrates rising from 2.3 million tonnes of fine copper this year to at least three million tonnes by 2000.
